sources.citation: Nikulin, Andrey. 2020. Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo. Tese de doutorado, Universidade de Brasília. xxiv+571 pp. §1.1.2 'Jaikó', p. 16; §3.2.1.12 (PMJ *k reflex in Jaikó); §3.3.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States the data are 'extremamente escassos, limitando-se a uma única lista de palavras coletada por Martius (1867, v. 1, p. 279; v. 2, p. 143)'; accepts only 13 items as genuinely Macro-Jê; reproduces Jaikó forms 'sem modificações'; treats Jaikó as a separate Macro-Jê family (Macro-Jê Oriental) on segmental grounds (reflex of PMJ *k appears as a coronal fricative).

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri; Vegini, Valdir; França, Maria Cristina Victorino de. 2015. Koropó, puri, kamakã e outras línguas do Leste Brasileiro: revisão e proposta de nova classificação. LIAMES 15(2): 223-277. doi:10.20396/liames.v15i2.8642302. Jaikó pp. 260-261.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Says 'só temos um vocabulário jaikó de 67 palavras (Martius, 1863, p. 143), que parece ser uma mistura de todas as línguas do Piauí' (Pimenteira/Karib, Masakará, Tupi, Maxakali look-alikes) and leaves Jaikó as 'Linguae Incertae Sedis'.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens. II. Zur Sprachenkunde (Wörtersammlung brasilianischer Sprachen / Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium). Leipzig: Friedrich Fleischer. Geicó wordlist p. 143.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The only primary data on the language: a 67-item Latin-Geicó wordlist on p. 143 with one footnote ('Vergl. I. 279. Die eingeschlossenen Buchstaben werden stumm mitgehört'). About 28 of the 67 forms carry an unexplained acute accent, mostly on the last vowel (uschiegkó, iquaté, ijahú, grangblá, maecó, aepurgó, ayanté, y(l)rouró, scharrepiú, scharrété, oopáung, namblú, aenettá, ná, já, ae(e)rú, juckqué, mandaltú, chügkrá, nempiaepiú, cärá, u(l)epú, aenaenongsiaé); Martius's only general remark on the acute (vol. 2 p. 29, in the introduction to the Tupi dictionary, not to this list) say…
